tips.comment: Well thought of and well found in the market when going off at just 7/2 in the Craven. Too keen for his own good in that race and is worth another chance down in grade here.
Previous course winner at Sandown, albeit over a furlong shorter. The horse has yet to see his colours lowered from three career starts, so the current 7-2 looks fair enough.
I thought Matauri Bay was very impressive on his debut. After running a 0.75L second in his last race, he's only beaten one horse home in both of his races since. Here's hoping he can bounce back.

I took the SP price on this colt with a bookie who's paying 3 places. He finished 3 lengths short LTO over 10 furlongs, but he's back down to a mile with first-time cheekpieces, and the price represents good value.

Roger Varian's trained colt should have progressed a lot at home since winning well at Epsom Downs on debut 13 months ago. He bids to remain unbeaten, so gets the nod, particularly as he should run well fresh and is unexposed.
This race is fairly open with all runners having good arguments to win. However, I fancy an each way bet on the visitor from abroad, Suhail Star, who could perhaps finish in the places.
Ran a cracker on reappearance in the Spring Mile last time. The form of that race has worked out well enough. Should run his race here.
Showed promise with her previous yard but bred to do much better. The switch to this stable could unlock further improvement, and she's well drawn. Big player.

Preference here goes to the Richard Hughes-trained Whip Cracker. Arrives with a bit to prove after two lesser efforts at Thirsk and Doncaster. First-time headgear is applied, and if that has a positive effect, then he could be a serious player dropping down in grade. Standout jockey booking, with Ryan Moore back on board. Potential remains after past exploits, which include a recent spin on the AW, where he posted a career-best RPR.

Crack Shot returns for another crack at this having been a decent 4th off a 6lb higher mark last year. He lacks the upside of some of the 4yo’s so is a risk in that sense, but he’s drawn well to get a good tow into the race which lacks an obvious front runner. He was never travelling when a 10/3 shot at Newmarket last time out. Now 1lb below his last winning mark, you have to forgive him that and hope he’s nicely tuned up for this. The trainers are 6/10 a place here with 4 wins in the last year, and Buick has a sound 9/19 place record when running for them.
No comment made

The Class 3 Whitsun Cup handicap is a competitive affair although nothing exceptional stands out. Jack Channon trained Arkhalia Flynn, a 4yo by Ulysses out of a Dutch Art mare, returns for the season. Three wins and three second place finishes from ten runs suggest a tough sort. George Bass (SR 16%) rides. Drawn in stall 8 and allotted 8 stone 12 pounds here, still looking well handicapped on a mark of 84. 12-1 price looks value for a stable that does particularly well with its handicappers at the mile trip (Johan springs to mind).
Denied the hat-trick when upped in trip to a mile and a half at Newcastle last month and could benefit from this drop in trip.
Big reappearance figure last year off a similar break. Is now 3lb lower than last win, which can only help him at Sandown. Trainer in good form. Can go close here.

First time Cheekpieces. Won for Aiden O'Brien in Ireland. Highly tried, but returned to form when narrowly beaten carrying 10-0 at Haydock. Fastest run-out speed in the field and should be suited by Sandown finish. Stall 7 - Handicaps over 8-10f where the horse finished in the first 4 LTO - +£35.44 to a £1 EW Stake. FS Rating 66.4 (3rd)
Has shown ability in the past, and two runs this year on all-weather should have brought him to the boil. Not badly in at the weights and could run well at a big price.
Big price, but the horse knows how to win alright and has class. Time and distance percentages are all in favor tonight.

Won over a mile on his racecourse debut on the AW but showed improved form on his return when losing out in a photo finish at Newmarket over 10f. Will stay further but still worth considering here kept to a similar trip.
The King's Falcon, being by Dubawi, could be well at home on this surface. That can see Harry Burns taking off three pounds, getting a strong run from this bay gelding.
An interesting contender on breeding, though may prefer further in time. The yard has good form with 2 winners from the last 4 starters, so could easily outrun these big odds.

There are two mediocre 4-year-olds in this field against a few 3-year-olds who all have to prove their worth. Action Packed has only had one run against a hot favorite and has every chance of improvement.
Tee Aitch Aye has not run too badly in his two maiden races so far for Ian Jardine. He needs to show massive improvement to feature here, but so do quite a few of the more fancied 3-year-olds.

Hill O Rue is a lightly raced improver with back-to-back placings in handicaps, showing promise despite setbacks. Up in trip today, he's bred to progress and looks a strong contender for further improvement.
Sweet Cecely has raced twice on turf, and both have been on good to firm ground. Tonight, she encounters good to soft, which can see her letting herself down, being a daughter of Sir Percy.
Big price, but I think it will run very well. On breeding, it needs at least this distance, and sire horses go well on soft. So it could surprise a few, but not me.

The trainer is looking good recently. Recent form doesn't look great, but Tootsie is dropping a grade here today, so could well capitalise against weaker competition. Could be the restart that's needed.

Straya lines up today after a solid fifth at Thirsk, where she was beaten just under four lengths. She now drops into Class 6 company and competes off a career-low mark of 55. With a favourable draw and a return to a more suitable surface, she could offer value in a wide-open field.

The fourth at Wolverhampton last time was an improvement on recent runs and an indicator that he looks ready to win again. The form of the Chester win last summer is the best of any in this field. The yard is in good form with five winners in the last two weeks. Dropped another pound and now a whopping forty-seven pounds below the highest mark.
Martin's Brig is a consistent, experienced runner with solid course form, a recent win, and proven ability in this class. Game and genuine, he stays the trip well and rates a strong contender today.

I'm not quite sure why Langholm is as short a price as he currently is, given his lack of any recent form. He normally races at Catterick, although he has won at Carlisle in the past. He has never raced at a mile; however, he does act on easy ground, which are the conditions he meets tonight.

Back down to a winning mark of 55, having won off this mark in August 2024 at Musselburgh. Will strip fitter for 2 runs in the last 5 weeks following a 6-month break and welcome the slight drop in trip, having raced over the extended mile at Nottingham on the 9th of May.

LOCKDOWN LASS is clearly well treated and may be capable of a revival with the yard in such fine form. She is a mature experienced type who has a solid enough back-profile relative to racing in this company and she merits a marke check.

Slipped to just 2lb above his last winning mark and looks dangerously well treated. Won over 7f at Musselburgh in April and wasn’t beaten far since despite racing prominently in tougher company. Back down to Class 6, where he's a dual winner, and drawn to attack from a handy position. If bouncing back to early-season form, he could surprise at a big price.

Has dropped back to her last winning mark and shaped with renewed promise when 3rd at Newcastle in March, setting the pace and only fading late. That effort showed signs of a revival, and she's now back after a break with conditions to suit. Turf form is solid and she’s one of the few here proven off this mark. Worth chancing at big odds, especially if allowed an easy lead.

The Willie Mullins forecast favorite doesn't look anything special on paper, so the selection is the Emmet Mullins-trained Barra Rua. She is related to numerous winners, including Coney Island, and going back to the prolific winners Rhinestone Cowboy and Wichita Lineman. The trainer has an exceptional 25% record in bumpers over the last 5 years, and top amateur jockey John Gleeson takes the ride.
The bumper has a Team Mullins debutant going to post but Im sticking with Betty Mo Chara who ran a decent race on debut finishing 4th at this track and should improve for that experience.

The model I run suggests an upset for Sing My Story. This result has been driven by Sing My Story having the highest RPR of this 14-runner field. All horses step out carrying the same initial weight, and Mr. Aherne on board relieves a further 7 lbs claiming. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

ALTO SAX is a ride for a bang-in-form apprentice jockey and Keithen Kennedy rode this four year old when showing up well at odds latest. He is a Saxon Warrior-sired four year old who returns to the scene of his course and distance win and should prove hard to contain.

Breathe Again started out in handicaps with a rating of 75. The handicapper has released his grip, which can see him being competitive off 65, ten pounds lower. He is three pounds lower from his last run at Gowran Park when third. James Ryan is in the saddle, who could be working the oracle for success.
Ok - goes well for a young female jockey - tick, course specialist - tick, coming here off a decent last time effort - tick, won't mind any rain - tick. That's enough reasons to have a decent bet.

Ranko Express didn't run too badly over hurdles on his most recent run, prior to that he'd been running well on the flat , he's versatile regards distance, good form between 1m1f - 1m3f so today's distance of 1m2f fits in nicely. His best efforts on the flat was from a lower rating than he is at the moment but this mark of 62 shouldn't over burden him , can be competitive , factor in the 7 lb claim by the jockey , he's not badly treated. Each-way tip.
No comment made

Rockbury Lad has won 3 times, the last coming at Bellewstown last month off a mark of 65. He was raised 5 lbs and was only 5th off that mark at Leopardstown 2 weeks ago but has already been dropped 3 lbs. He looks a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.
No comment made
Takeachancejimmy ran a good race and only came short by a short head at Bellewstown with S Wallace on board. He retains the ride.

Been running well and wasn’t beaten far over 7f at Gowran three starts ago despite finishing in midfield. Raced off the same mark next time at Roscommon when beaten by the smallest of margins. Below that level back there last time when unsuited by the way the race developed, slowly run. Goes up in distance here and if they go a good gallop can return to winning ways.
Caught the eye on penultimate start having done best of those up with the pace, though disappointed last time. Drops 3lb and moves up in trip. Trained by wily old Murtagh. Worth an each-way bet.

1st reserve BARRYS ROCK seldom runs a bad race here at Fairyhouse. He somehow keeps his best form for here. Was placed 4 times here the last 2 seasons off higher marks than this. Has run well fresh here too when 2nd here off a winter break 2 seasons back. That’s all the good stuff. The bad stuff is he’s 10 and still a maiden, and others bring way more form to the table. But at 33/1, I’ll have a wild swing.

A 3-time winner on the flat when trained abroad. Pulled up a furlong out on race debut for this yard on a maiden hurdle at Fairyhouse last month and then finished 8th in a flat handicap over 1m2f at Roscommon in a better race than this 10 days ago when fading in the final furlong. The stable is in good form and amongst the winners with 2 from the last 4 starts, so could do better today at an each-way price with 5 places.

The change of stables did the trick for the now Gavin Cromwell trained Flying Fortress who scored decisively earlier this month at Ballinrobe. The selection looks capable of much better on that display.

Arrives to this race a beaten favorite, and trainer Joseph Patrick O'Brien runs this one with jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle, indicating first string. Also, The Marty Party could be in the mix at the finish. Joseph Patrick O'Brien could be having the first two home for the forecast to pay handsomely.

Winston Junior is of interst here.The selection is after three runs now and steps into handicap company for the first time and that after being supported in his three runs so far.He looks to be on a good mark on handicap bow and can run a big race.

Sugar Club is worth chancing at these odds as an each way bet. Representing the Noel Meade/Colin Keane combination, Sugar Club ran well from out of the weights when 4th at Naas this month. A repeat of that can see the selection place this evening.

A six-race maiden, she looked unlucky last time at Ballinrobe when having anything but a trouble-free run at crucial times in the race. That was in an extended 9f maiden and looks interesting here over 10f, back in handicap company from a 9lb lower mark than her last start in one.

Huge price for a runner from this yard. Fairly consistent last season and forgiven comeback flop which was on heavy ground. Hugh Horgan takes 5lb off and has place chances at least if anywhere near his best.

West Of Carrig has not had much luck, not staying over three miles and one furlong at Tipperary, fell at Cork, and unseated Mr. A J Browne at Cheltenham in the Challenge Cup won by Wonderwall. The son of Westerner is coming back in distance with staying over hurdles. That can see making a serious mark and there has been market support which should be noted.

HARD TARGET showed more in a big field latest likely in need of the run. Assuming that decent effort has helped and he steps forward he is a well handicapped runner who van be given some sort of chance at double-figure odds in this modest looking handicap.

YOUKNOWHATIMEAN runs for a trainer/jockey combination already seen to winning effect at this venue today. The trainer's runners are respected at Limerick and this well treated racer could bounce back from an unseat latest. Value call.

Love Me Tender has been entered up in a few races recently but pulled out late on, presumably due to the ground. He is nicely bred being by Doctor Dino and out of a good French mare who also produced the very promising Kainsbourg, trained by Gordon Elliott. He looks like he should be another winner for Willie Mullins.

The model I run suggests an upset from Mollys Dolly. This result has been driven by Mollys Dolly having the joint highest RPR of this 12-runner field. The weights being carried all look reasonably similar, but Mollys Dolly does carry the joint lowest weight here. Tries the tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator for this as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

The model I run suggests Itsalonglongroad can win this one. This result has been driven by Itsalonglongroad having the highest RPR of the smaller 7-runner field. Itsalonglongroad has one of the lower official rankings here, meaning he looks well treated on this weight. Goes out carrying far less weight than the two current market leaders who are top of the weights. This is a weight differential of over 1 stone. Itsalonglongroad is a prior course and distance winner here and looks to get the job done again over this 1m 7.5f trip. The model has issued a 'low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This result has been driven by the combination of a small win probability % gap back to second, but the reasonable value on offer here at 10s.

The model I run suggests an upset from Star In The Park. The result has been driven predominantly by Star In The Park having the second highest RPR of this 12-runner field and is not penalized for it in weights. All horses go out carrying the same initial weight, but Star In The Park has Gavin Brouder on board relieving 3 lbs. Ran very recently, so race fitness is not a concern. The model thinks this is materially mispriced and is the value play here. 21s also does offer the 'each way' angle if you prefer that betting style. The model has issued a 'very high' staking indicator for this, which translates to a 4pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is predominantly driven by the perceived mispricing relative to the win probability %.

The model I run suggests Wonleg can win this race. Wonleg lines up here with the highest RPR of the runners in this field. All horses go out carrying the same amount of initial weight, bar two outsiders. Wonleg is a previous distance winner over this 2m trip. Last run 22 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Two Become One can win this one. This result has been driven by Two Become One having a relatively higher RPR compared to the rest of the field, and all horses go out carrying the same weights. Two Become One last ran 18 days ago after a break and probably needed the run out. Quick turnaround here and looks to build on that performance. Two Become One's trainer, Gordon Elliott, has a high RTF %. The model has issued a 'high' staking indicator here, which translates to a 2pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is a result of the value on offer at 13s relative to the win probability % generated by the model.

The model I run suggests The Border Boy can cause an upset here. The Border Boy lines up with the highest RPR of this larger 16-horse race but goes out with the lowest official ranking. This suggests the weight being carried is lower than the horse's potential. The Border Boy carries over a stone less than some of the current market leaders, and that could be telling over this slightly longer 2m 5f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

The model I run suggests Star Official can win this race. This result has been driven by Star Official having the highest RPR of the 8 runner field. This horse also goes out with the second lowest official ranking, which translates to the second lowest weight being carried around this 2m trip. Star Official last ran 46 days ago and is a prior course and distance winner, so no concerns around ability to get the job done at this course or race fitness. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
